text_blocks.snippet: The annual inflation rate in the United States, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), was 2.7% for the 12 months ending June 2025. This is up from 2.4% in the 12 months ending May. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (.gov) will release the next update on August 12th, covering the 12 months ending July.

list.snippet: Headline Inflation: The CPI for all items rose 2.7% over the past 12 months, indicating an overall increase in the cost of goods and services.

Core Inflation: Prices for all items less food and energy rose by 2.9% over the same period. This excludes the more volatile food and energy prices and provides a clearer picture of underlying inflation trends.
